Quick start: your first assessment in 10 minutes

1. Define the workplace. On the Stations page, use “Edit workplace” to enter the workplace name, address and assessor. These appear on the cover of the Excel and PDF reports.
  2. Add a station and a task. Add the station (e.g. Shipping dock) with “+ Station” and the task (e.g. Palletising) with “+ Task” on the station card. Entering the task’s time in the shift (min) makes the daily exposure and risk table more accurate.
  3. Choose the method. If you’re not sure, answer a few questions in the Guide; it shows the recommended method for each risk area and why.
  4. Do the analysis and save it. Use Posture analysis if you have a video or photo, the Forms page if you have measurements or observations. Choose the station and task in the box before saving.
  5. Open an action. After saving, “+ Action” appears next to each suggestion under the result. Assign an owner and a due date.
  6. Get the report. Download a PDF or Excel from the Stations page.

Field mode: collect first, analyse later

Analysing every job on the spot takes time. Field mode separates observation from assessment.

  1. On the Field page choose the station and task (if you don’t know, leave it empty and choose later with “Edit”).
  2. Use 📷 Photo to take a picture with the phone camera or choose from the gallery. There can be several photos.
  3. If you shot a video, open it with 🎞 Grab a video frame, go to the important moments and press “Add this frame”. Frames are stored with their video time.
  4. Mark the hazards you saw (lifting, pushing-pulling, repetitive work…). If you know them, enter the load, repetitions per shift and task duration.
  5. Add a note. You can dictate with the microphone on the phone keyboard.
  6. “Save field record”. The record goes to the Awaiting analysis list.

Back at your desk, the record in the list shows method buttons for the hazards you marked (e.g. Lifting → NIOSH, KIM-LHC). Pressing a button selects the station/task and carries the load and frequency into the form. The “Posture” button on a photo opens that frame in posture analysis. The analyses you save are linked to the field record; mark it “Completed” when done.

Photos are stored in the browser database on the device (IndexedDB) and never uploaded. Only thumbnails go into the JSON backup.

1. Open the file with “Choose a video or photo”. In a video, go to the most demanding moment with the slider and the ±1 frame and ±1 s buttons (←/→ on the keyboard, with Shift for 1 s).
  2. Press “Analyse this frame”. Choose the direction the person faces.
  3. Tap the 8 points in the order the on-screen hint gives: ear, shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand, hip, knee, ankle. Drag a wrong point to correct it; to re-place a specific point, select it below.
  4. The angles are calculated automatically. If you measured an angle with a goniometer, type it into the table; the value you type shows in orange and is used.
  5. Mark the observations: load, coupling, legs, twisting, static posture, repetition. All three methods use this information.
  6. Choose the task and save. Save several frames of the same task; the station card shows the timeline and the worst value.

For a good recording: hold the camera side-on and level to the person, keep the whole body in view, and record at least 2–3 work cycles. If you’ll measure distances, have a reference (pallet, door, tape measure) in the frame.

Converts pixels in the video to centimetres; you get measurements such as the NIOSH horizontal (H) and vertical (V) distance, reach distance or bench height from the image without a tape measure.

  1. Press “📏 Measure distance” in posture analysis, the 📏 button next to a centimetre field in the forms, or the 📏 in a field record.
  2. Reference: Tap both ends of an object of known length (Euro pallet 120 × 80 cm, door frame, A4 paper, the worker’s stature). Choose it from the list or type the real length.
  3. Measure: Tap the start and end of the distance you want to measure (or press and drag). Each measurement shows its length and horizontal and vertical components. A magnifier appears while dragging.
  4. If you opened it from a form, carry the value into the field with a button such as “H = 42 cm”. Horizontal fields use the horizontal component, height fields the vertical component.

1. Choose the method on the Forms page. For lifting, switching between uniform / different loads is the button at the top of the method.
  2. Fill in the fields; the result and suggestions update instantly as you type. How to measure is written under each field.
  3. Choose the task and press “Save”. After saving you can open “+ Action” from the suggestions; to correct the same record, change it and press “Save changes”.

Less used or older methods (KIM 2001, Strain Index, HAL, noise, vibration, heat, lighting…) appear when “Show advanced methods” is on.

1. Open an action with “+ Action” on a suggestion of a saved analysis; the title and description come from the suggestion and the current result is stored as “before”.
  2. Enter the action type (elimination, technical, administrative, PPE, training), owner and due date. Open actions past their due date show in red.
  3. When the action is implemented, press “Re-measure” on the action card: the form opens with the old inputs; correct the changed conditions and save.
  4. The card shows the before → after difference and the “improved / same / worsened” result. The risk map always uses the latest measurement.

The table on the Stations page makes each risk area of each station a row. Choose Fine-Kinney or the 5×5 matrix with the button at the top.

  • Suggested values: probability comes from the method’s risk level, frequency from the task duration (120 min or more per shift is “continuous”), severity from the hazard type.
  • Correct: use “Edit” to change the hazard, possible harm, probability, frequency and severity for the workplace. A changed row is marked “corrected by hand”; undo it with “Back to suggested values”.
  • The scale values come from common practice; compare them with your organisation’s own table.

When you enter the tasks’ times in the shift (min), the station card shows the shift profile: each task’s share of the shift, the time-weighted share of high-risk postures (REBA and OWAS) and a sub-activity table for the other methods. Tasks without a duration get equal weight, and this is stated on screen.

• PDF report (PDF on the Stations page or a station card): cover, executive summary, risk map, risk table, station details, action plan, methods and signature fields.
  • Excel: summary, risk table, action plan, results and method sheets; the station file contains each record’s A4 form (with photos).
  • CSV: one method result per row; for Power BI or pivots.
  • For the first PDF/Excel the library is loaded once from the internet; without a connection the download does not work.
Where is the data, how do I back it up?

• All records are stored in the browser on this device; they are not sent to a server. If you clear the browser data, the records are deleted too.
  • Backup: “Copy JSON” on the Stations page is a full backup; paste it into a file and keep it. On another device, merge it with “Import JSON” (the same record is not added twice).
  • Full-size field photos do not go into the backup, only thumbnails.
  • If storage fills up, the app drops the full frames, keeps thumbnails and warns you. You can clear old records after exporting them to Excel.
  • If several people need to work with the same data or a central backup is needed, the app has to run on a server.
